topic: How does the 14.6% bandwidth affect frequency planning for multi-satellite networks with adjacent channel interference risks?
consensus_response: The 14.6% bandwidth within Ku-band exacerbates inter-satellite interference, leading to increased signal attenuation and reduced network capacity due to shared frequencies.  This necessitates careful frequency planning strategies like dynamic allocation, spectrum sharing agreements, and AMC modulation techniques for optimal resource utilization and minimized interference. Advanced modulation techniques like OFDM can separate data streams across multiple frequencies within a single channel, improving spectral efficiency and mitigating interference.
reference_context: Satellite communication systems utilize a limited number of available frequencies in the Ku-band to support inter-satellite links. Shared spectrum raises the likelihood of adjacent channel interference, impacting network performance through signal degradation.  Effective frequency planning is critical for minimizing interference and maximizing spectral efficiency within multi-satellite networks.
